# Detection rules

<!-- generated by scripts/lib/gen-catalogue.mjs; do not edit by hand -->

45 rules. Severity weights: critical 12, major 6, minor 2 points.
Each extra occurrence adds 25% of the weight, capped at 2x. Score = sum of points, max 100.
Verdict: **heavy** at 35 or more; **clean** below 10 with no critical finding; otherwise **light**.

Where: `desktop` = 1440 px, `mobile` = 390 px, `css` rules read the stylesheet text.

## spacing

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spacing-off-grid` | minor | desktop | Padding and gaps ignore a 4 px rhythm. Values like 13, 18 or 22 px show that spacing was typed, not chosen from a scale. | Pick a 4 px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64) and snap every padding and gap to the nearest step. |
| `spacing-cramped` | minor | desktop+mobile | Text sits against the edge of its box. Buttons and cards with almost no inner padding read as unfinished. | Give buttons at least 12 px horizontal and 8 px vertical padding (anything under 8 px horizontal is flagged), cards at least 16 px. |

## color

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color-purple-gradient` | critical | desktop | Violet / indigo gradient. The purple-to-blue gradient is the most recognisable AI-product colour move. | Replace with one flat brand colour. If depth is needed, use a surface step and a 1 px line, not a gradient. |
| `color-gradient-text` | major | desktop | Gradient-filled text. Headings or numbers clipped to a colour ramp are a stock "AI landing" signature. | Set the text in one solid colour; emphasise with size, weight or position instead. |
| `color-glow` | major | desktop | Coloured glow shadow. Large zero-offset shadows in a saturated colour fake "energy" and hurt legibility. | Use a neutral, low-alpha shadow with a real offset, or no shadow and a 1 px border. |
| `color-low-contrast` | major | desktop+mobile | Text below WCAG contrast. Grey-on-tint and pale-on-white text fails readers and audits alike. | Darken the text (or lighten the surface) until body text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1. |
| `color-framework-default` | major | desktop | Stock framework palette. Untouched indigo/violet/slate swatches from popular utility palettes make unrelated products look alike. | Derive the palette from the brand: one accent chosen on purpose, neutrals tinted toward it. |

## icons

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon-tile` | major | desktop | Icon in a rounded coloured tile, repeated. A tinted square with a glyph above a heading is the default feature-card opener. | Drop the tile. Use a bare icon at one size, or no icon and let the heading carry the card. |
| `icon-emoji-ui` | major | desktop | Emoji used as interface icons. Emoji in headings, buttons and list items render differently per platform and signal a quick draft. | Use one consistent line-icon set (one size, one stroke width) or remove the glyph. |

## copy

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `copy-cliche` | major | desktop | Stock marketing vocabulary. Words such as "seamless", "elevate" or "unleash" carry no information and mark the text as generated. | Say the concrete thing: what the product does, for whom, with what number or example. |
| `copy-contrast-formula` | major | desktop | "Not X, but Y" headline formula. Defining the product by what it is not ("not just a tool, it's a partner") is a reflex of generated copy. | State the claim directly: say what it is and what the reader gets. |
| `copy-em-dash` | minor | desktop | Em dashes scattered through the copy. Three or more em dashes on one page is a frequent sign of generated prose. | Split the sentence, or use a comma, colon or full stop. |
| `copy-trailing-period` | minor | desktop | Full stops on short UI text. Headings, buttons and labels do not end in a full stop; paragraphs do. | Remove the final full stop from headings, buttons, labels and captions of one sentence. |
| `copy-greeting` | minor | desktop | Greeting as a page heading. "Welcome back, Sam" names no context; the heading should say what this screen is. | Name the content ("This month's scans"), not the visitor. |
| `copy-placeholder` | critical | desktop | Placeholder or filler text left in. Lorem ipsum, "Acme", "John Doe" and [bracketed] gaps show the page was never finished. | Write the real text, or remove the block. Never ship a stand-in name. |
| `copy-unverified-proof` | major | desktop | Social proof with no source. Round user counts, star scores and "trusted by" lines that cannot be checked read as invented. | Cite the source and date, link to the real logo or review, or delete the claim. |

## typography

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type-reflex-font` | minor | desktop | Reflex font family. Inter, Poppins, Space Grotesk and a few others are what models pick without a reason. | Choose a family on purpose and write the reason in DESIGN.md. A system stack is better than an unexamined default. |
| `type-flat-hierarchy` | major | desktop | Flat type hierarchy. When the largest text is barely bigger than body text, nothing leads the eye. | Set a scale with clear steps: at least 2x between page title and body, and visible steps between heading levels. |
| `type-eyebrow` | major | desktop | Eyebrow label above the heading. A small, spaced, uppercase tag above every heading is a template habit. | Delete it, or fold the information into the heading. Keep at most one, and only if it carries a fact. |
| `type-tight-leading` | minor | desktop+mobile | Body text set too tight. Multi-line paragraphs under 1.3 line-height, or letter-spacing below -0.04em, are hard to read. | Body line-height 1.5 to 1.7; keep tight leading for headings only and never track tighter than -0.03em. |
| `type-long-measure` | minor | desktop | Line length above 85 characters. Very long lines make the eye lose its place. | Cap running text at 60 to 75 characters (max-width: 65ch). |
| `type-heavy-weight` | minor | desktop | Heavy weights carry the hierarchy. Weights of 800 to 900, or bold on most text, flatten emphasis. Hierarchy should come from size and colour. | Use 400 and 500 (600 sparingly). Let size and tone do the ranking. |

## layout

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `layout-nested-cards` | major | desktop | Card inside a card. Boxes within boxes add borders and shadows but no information. | Keep one container. Group inside it with spacing, a divider or a heading. |
| `layout-identical-cards` | major | desktop | Row of identical icon + title + text cards. Three or four same-size feature cards in a row say nothing about which point matters. | Rank the points: one larger block for the main idea, the rest as a list or table. |
| `layout-stat-strip` | major | desktop | Row of big numbers with small labels. A strip of three or four headline metrics without a comparison is the standard hero-metric template. | Show one number that matters most, with its comparison base and date; move the rest into a table or chart. |
| `layout-side-stripe` | major | desktop | Coloured stripe down one side of a box. A thick left border on a card, alert or quote is a common AI shortcut for emphasis. | Emphasise with a tinted surface, a heading or an icon. Do not use a one-sided accent border. |
| `layout-overflow-x` | critical | desktop+mobile | Page scrolls sideways. Horizontal overflow is a bug, most often on phones. | Find the widest element, give it max-width: 100% or let it wrap; do not hide the overflow on body. |
| `layout-tap-target` | minor | mobile | Touch targets under 32 px. Small buttons and links are hard to hit on a phone. | Make every control at least 44 px tall (minimum 32 px) with padding rather than larger text. |

## detail

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detail-pulse-dot` | major | desktop | Pulsing status dot. A blinking "live" dot on a status that never changes pretends the product is alive. | Show status only when it comes from data, as text plus colour, without animation. |
| `detail-glass` | minor | desktop | Frosted glass on several surfaces. Backdrop blur on many elements costs performance and rarely has anything meaningful behind it. | Use solid surfaces. Keep blur for at most one overlay that really sits over content. |
| `detail-announce-pill` | major | desktop | Announcement pill above the hero heading. A rounded "New: ..." badge above the h1 is on nearly every generated landing page. | Remove it. If there is real news, link it in the header or footer. |
| `detail-numbered` | minor | desktop | Decorative section numbers. "01 / 02 / 03" on content that has no sequence is ornament. | Number only real steps (use an ordered list). Otherwise drop the numbers. |
| `detail-arrow-links` | minor | desktop | Arrow glyph on many links. Appending "→" to every link and button is decoration. | Keep an arrow only on the single primary action, if direction carries meaning. |
| `detail-card-triple` | minor | desktop | Border, soft shadow and tint on every card. Stacking a border, a diffuse shadow and a different fill on the same surface is three signals for one idea. | Pick one separator per surface: a border, or a tint, or (for floating layers only) a shadow. |
| `detail-focus-ring` | major | css | Focus outline removed without a replacement. Keyboard users cannot see where they are. | Add :focus-visible with a 2 px outline (or ring) in an accent colour; never leave outline: none alone. |
| `detail-hover-lift` | minor | css | Cards lift or grow on hover. translateY(-4px) and scale(1.05) on hover is a stock micro-interaction. | Change tone or border colour on hover, only inside @media (hover: hover). |

## imagery

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image-blur-blob` | major | desktop | Blurred colour blob behind the content. Soft coloured orbs in the hero background are decoration without subject. | Remove the blob. If the hero needs an image, use a real photo, product screen or diagram. |
| `image-placeholder-src` | critical | desktop | Stand-in image service. Placeholder or random-photo URLs (placehold, picsum, pravatar ...) show an unfinished page and may disappear. | Replace with the real asset hosted with the site, or remove the slot. |
| `image-avatar-stack` | major | desktop | Overlapping avatar row. A stack of round faces beside "trusted by" is the stock proof device, and the faces are rarely real. | Replace with a named customer quote that can be checked, or remove. |
| `image-no-alt` | minor | desktop | Image without an alt attribute. Screen readers announce the file name instead of the meaning; alt="" marks decoration explicitly. | Write a short description, or alt="" if the image is purely decorative. |
| `image-broken` | major | desktop | Image fails to load. A broken image icon is an obvious defect. | Fix the path or remove the element. |

## motion

| Rule | Severity | Where | What it catches | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `motion-infinite` | major | desktop | Ornament that animates forever. Endless loops (floating shapes, shimmering text, tickers) compete with content and drain batteries. | Animate in response to an action and then stop. Keep infinite loops for real loading indicators only. |
| `motion-entrance-everywhere` | minor | desktop | Everything fades up on load or scroll. Six or more elements entering with the same fade-and-rise turns motion into wallpaper. | Animate one moment (the hero, or one key reveal). Leave the rest still. |
| `motion-no-reduced` | minor | css | No prefers-reduced-motion handling. People who ask the system for less motion still get all of it. | Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that removes or shortens animations and transitions. |
| `motion-transition-all` | minor | css | transition: all. Animating every property triggers layout work and surprising effects. | List the properties you mean (opacity, transform, background-color) with a duration and easing. |
